facebook.content_angle: Hand entry and catch position errors — how a poor hand entry angle creates immediate drag and costs measurable split-time losses that most swimmers repeat thousands of times per session without realising it
facebook.post_text:
A bad hand entry angle costs you speed before your catch even begins. 🌊

Most competitive swimmers focus on their pull phase — but the damage is already done the moment your hand hits the water at the wrong angle. You're creating drag on every single stroke, thousands of times a session.

👉 Entering thumb-first or with a wide elbow flares your hand outward and pushes water sideways instead of forward
👉 The correct entry is fingertips first, hand angled slightly inward at 10–15 degrees, elbow high and relaxed
👉 Even a 5-degree correction reduces frontal drag and sets up a deeper, more powerful early catch position

Fix the entry — and the catch takes care of itself. 🎯

✔️ Drill it: fingertip drag drill — drag fingertips along the surface before entry to train a high-elbow, forward-angled hand path
✔️ Film yourself from underwater — entry errors are nearly invisible from the deck but obvious on camera
✔️ One session of focused entry work can shift your distance-per-stroke before your next race block

Where does your hand enter the water — inside your shoulder line, outside, or right on the money?
